Fit a bivariate response surface

Source: R/layers-stats-surfaces.R
stat_smooth_3d.Rd

Fits a model of z on x and y in each group and draws its predictions on an x/y grid. As in ggplot2::stat_smooth(), method is a fitting function or its name, called as method(formula, data = data, weights = weight, ...) with method.args in ..., and the surface is predict(fit, newdata, se.fit = ). Any model with such a predict() method works: thin-plate or tensor-product smooths from mgcv, robust or generalised linear models, random forests. Fitting functions see transformed x, y and z. The default formula is z ~ x + y; "gam" uses z ~ s(x, y) from mgcv, and loess takes span.

Usage

stat_smooth_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  method = "loess",
  formula = NULL,
  n = 30L,
  se = TRUE,
  level = 0.95,
  span = 0.75,
  method.args = list(),
  se.alpha = 0.2,
  domain = c("box", "hull"),
  view = NULL,
  cond = list(),
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

geom_smooth_3d(...)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

method

A fitting function, the name of one ("loess", "lm", "gam", "glm", ...), or a fitted model with a predict() method. "gam" requires mgcv.

formula

Model formula in x, y and z, for a fitting function.

n

Grid resolution, a scalar or two integers.

se

Confidence display: "surfaces" (or TRUE) draws translucent lower and upper surfaces; "band" closes them with walls along the edge of the domain into one translucent volume around the fit; "fill" draws the fit alone, filled by the standard error unless fill is mapped or set; "none" (or FALSE) draws the fit alone.

level

Pointwise confidence level.

span

Loess span.

method.args

Named arguments passed to the fitting function.

se.alpha

Opacity multiplier for confidence surfaces and walls.

domain

"box" fills the x/y range of the panel; "hull" clips the surface to the convex hull of the group's observations, so the model is not drawn where it extrapolates. Grid cells crossed by the hull edge are cut along it and the model is evaluated on the cut.

view

For a fitted model, the names of its predictors drawn on x and y.

cond

For a fitted model, a named list holding a value for each other predictor.

Details

method may instead be a model fitted beforehand. It is evaluated in data units: the grid's x and y are back-transformed and named by view, the predictions are transformed by the z scale. When view is NULL it takes the variable names of the layer's x and y mappings, if these are bare column names, else c("x", "y"). Other predictors of the model take the values in cond, or by default the observed value closest to the median and the most frequent level, as in mgcv::vis.gam().

Bounds are pointwise confidence intervals for the conditional mean, with Student t quantiles on the residual degrees of freedom, and normal quantiles on the link scale mapped through the inverse link for glm fits, as in ggplot2.

Computed variables

surface

"fit", "lower", "upper", and "side" for the walls of a band.

se

Standard error of the fitted mean on the model's scale (link scale for glm fits), averaged over each triangle.

z_mean

Transformed mean height of each triangle.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8))
d$z <- with(d, x + y + sin(3*x*y) / 5)
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_smooth_3d(method = "lm", n = 12) + coord_3d()
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  stat_smooth_3d(method = "lm", se = FALSE, n = 8) + coord_3d()

# A fitting function with its own formula: a quadratic response surface
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_smooth_3d(method = lm, formula = z ~ poly(x, y, degree = 2),
    se = "band", n = 12) + coord_3d()

# A model fitted beforehand, drawn over the hull of the data and filled by
# its standard error
fit <- lm(mpg ~ poly(wt, 2) + hp, data = mtcars)
ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, hp, z = mpg)) +
  geom_smooth_3d(method = fit, domain = "hull", se = "fill", n = 20) +
  geom_point_3d() + coord_3d()
